title: Modelled rain pore pressure did not change shallow Kilauea earthquake rates or swarm onsets in 1986-2025, and long-record windward gauges show no extreme rain before the 2018 eruption
abstract: Farquharson and Amelung (2020) proposed that rain water increased pore pressure at 1-3 km depth and triggered the May 2018 Kilauea rift eruption. Poland et al. (2022) disagreed. We tested the seismic prediction of this mechanism with USGS ComCat earthquakes (M 1.5+, 1980-2026) and NOAA GHCN-Daily rain. We modelled the rain pore-pressure anomaly with 1-D diffusion for 30 models (two kernels, D 0.01-1 m2/s, depth 1-3 km). January-April 2018 rain was 1.11-1.37 times the mean at four long-record windward gauges (ranks 6-27); only a 4-year summit gauge gave 2.2. With Hilo rain, the modelled pressure on 30 April 2018 was at the 3rd-84th percentile of the previous 50 years. High-passed monthly counts in the shallow summit and East Rift Zone did not follow modelled pressure: r was -0.084 to +0.071 in 1986-2018, and the family-wise p against 73 year-shifted rain records was 0.54 or more; 2019-2025 and a summit gauge gave the same result. For 1986-2018, 95% upper bounds on the rate change per standard deviation of pressure (0.69 kPa in the step model with D 0.1 m2/s at 2 km) were +9% to +24% for summit and combined regions and up to +50% for the East Rift Zone alone. Catalogue swarm onsets did not occur at high modelled pressure (family-wise p 0.18 or more), and wet-season onset rate ratios were above or below 1 depending on the season definition. Limitations: single gauges, a simple diffusion model, a live catalogue with magnitude changes, and low power for effects near 20% per standard deviation.

display.caption: (a) January-April rain divided by the station mean at four long-record windward gauges; 2018 is circled. (b, c) Modelled rain pore-pressure anomaly at 2 km depth from Hilo rain for three diffusivities, step and pulse kernels; red line: eruption onset on 3 May 2018.

Correlation of high-passed monthly log earthquake counts with high-passed modelled pore pressure for 30 models per region and magnitude threshold, 1986-2018 and 2019-2025. No single-model test had p < 0.05 against 73 year-shifted rain records; family-wise p values are at the right.

Left: monthly distribution of 75 shallow summit and East Rift Zone swarm onsets (1986 to April 2018) with Hilo mean monthly rain. Right: wet-season to dry-season onset rate ratios with exact 95% intervals for two season definitions; the red dotted line marks a ratio of 2.
